PullRequest.Title: chat: fix GitHub context repository selection
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes GitHub issue and pull request attachment selection across the Agents window and editor window.

- avoid waiting on unresolved local Git metadata before opening GitHub context in the Agents window
- in a multi-root editor workspace, choose a workspace folder before resolving its GitHub repository
- pass unresolved folder selections to Copilot Chat so the Issue/Pull Request search remains repository-scoped
- resolve remotes without waiting for repository `HEAD` state, including direct `.git/config` lookup
- support Git worktrees by following their `gitdir` and `commondir` pointers
- preserve normal remote preference ordering and folder identity
- add regressions for unresolved local metadata, different multi-root repositories, multiple roots of the same repository, and folder-based repository resolution

Fixes #334603

Validation:
- `npm run transpile-client`
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/actions/chatContext.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/copilotChatSessions/test/browser/copilotChatSessionsProvider.test.ts` (92 passing)
- `npm --prefix extensions/copilot run test:unit -- src/extension/chatSessions/vscode-node/test/copilotCloudSessionsProvider.spec.ts` (37 passing)
- `npm --prefix extensions/copilot run typecheck`
- live Code OSS verification with a two-folder workspace: Issue and Pull Request searches for both a normal Git repository and a Git worktree were scoped exclusively to the selected repository

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed boundary call, hot transitive callers, no-cache startup condition, and per-file scaling are explicit in code and tests. Exact wall-clock impact varies by filesystem latency, so severity is medium rather than high.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The added stat runs once for every uncached local URI passed to getRepositoryFetchUrls; before Git discovery settles, content-exclusion verdicts deliberately are not memoized, so concurrent file checks scale the new I/O with files and checks rather than repositories.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: excessive filesystem I/O and increased completion, search, review, and prompt latency during Git discovery, especially on network-mounted workspaces
Findings.PreviousBehavior: getRepositoryFetchUrls first joined the shared initial-discovery promise. For an opened repository it then returned Git API state without filesystem I/O; unresolved files reached only the existing fallback stat after discovery.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every file-scheme URI now performs and awaits workspace.fs.stat before joining discovery, even when the URI is a file and therefore cannot take the new direct .git/config branch.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 201 newly adds `await vscode.workspace.fs.stat(uri)` ahead of the shared discovery wait. No equivalent filesystem operation existed on the opened-repository fast path before the PR.
Findings.Title: Gate the direct config probe to repository-root callers
Findings.Impact: While repository discovery is pending, content exclusion calls this API for each file and does not cache unsettled verdicts; collection-based prompt/search/review paths can therefore launch a burst of one extra stat per file on their critical path. Warm repository-root and verdict caches reduce later calls, but do not protect this startup window.
Findings.Evidence: RemoteContentExclusion.isIgnored calls getRepositoryFetchUrls on each repo-cache miss (extensions/copilot/src/platform/ignore/node/remoteContentExclusion.ts:187-195), explicitly avoids memoizing while discovery is unsettled (lines 263-271), and documents that a render can request hundreds of verdicts (lines 112-119). Its tests prove repeated Git lookups before discovery and concurrent multi-repository lookups. Numerous completion, search, review, and prompt call sites invoke isCopilotIgnored, including collection paths using Promise.all. The added line awaits a filesystem stat for all local URIs; for normal file inputs the result is not a directory, so this work cannot contribute to the direct-config optimization and execution falls through to the prior flow.
Findings.Recommendation: Restrict the direct .git/config fast path to callers that know they are passing a selected repository/workspace root (for example via a root-specific method or option), leaving generic file-based getRepositoryFetchUrls calls on the Git API/discovery path without this preflight stat.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Folder-based GitHub context resolution previously called getRepositoryFetchUrls, which eagerly awaited the shared initial Git repository discovery before reading remotes; that wait is bounded only after 30 seconds and discovery itself waits for every repository HEAD to initialize.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Opening the Issue or Pull Request context picker for a selected local folder could be blocked for up to 30 seconds when local Git HEAD metadata remained unresolved.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The new local repository-root fast path reads `.git/config` (including worktree pointers) and returns remote URLs before waitForInitialDiscovery, so the picker can proceed without waiting for HEAD/discovery.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: The changed Agents-window path passes its single local folder URI to the extension command; resolveGitHubContextRepository calls getRepositoryFetchUrls. RIGHT lines 200-216 now read and return direct config before the still-existing wait at line 226. waitForInitialDiscovery shares a raceTimeout with INITIAL_DISCOVERY_TIMEOUT_MS=30,000, while initial discovery waits for every repository HEAD. The added unresolved-metadata tests exercise the URI pass-through path. Base blame identifies commit 88a8ef6f793d1b593b47862bd00aab36e88b0733 as introducing the old wait on base line 202.

Scenarios.Scenario: Attach an Issue or Pull Request from the Agents window for a single local folder whose Git HEAD metadata is unresolved
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The browse action chooses the current folder, dispatches the extension command, resolves that folder to a GitHub repository, and only then opens and populates the GitHub search picker. Repository resolution and the initial GitHub search are on the user-visible critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch the open-issue/open-pull-request extension command with the selected repository string or folder URI.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One command per user browse action, plus at most one repository-picker command when no folder/repository can be selected directly.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same context command was dispatched, but the core side first attempted to open/resolve the local Git repository and passed a string repository id.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The command must resolve before the context workspace can be created.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stat the selected root and `.git`, then read `.git/config`; worktrees additionally read the gitdir pointer and `commondir`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: For one normal repository, two stats and one config read; a worktree adds pointer and common-directory reads. One probe per browse action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No direct pre-discovery config probe existed; resolution joined initial Git discovery and could wait up to 30 seconds.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These operations must finish before the picker opens, but replace/bypass a Git discovery wait of up to 30 seconds.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Search GitHub issues or pull requests scoped to the resolved repository.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initial search and at most one search per settled debounced query.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same GitHub search ran after repository selection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The initial result list waits on this request; picker creation itself follows only repository resolution.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Exactly one selected folder and, after the picker opens, one initial query plus debounced user queries; remote count is normally small and scanned sequentially.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Repository resolution is serialized before picker creation. The initial search is one request; later input is debounced by 300 ms and generation-guarded, although an older network request is not physically cancelled.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The new direct `.git/config` read is not cached. It intentionally bypasses the shared cold Git-discovery promise. GitHub search results have no local cache in this path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the URI pass-through, direct config return before waitForInitialDiscovery, and serialized command/search flow are explicit and tested.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Local config reads are usually fast; the fixed delay is largest only when Git discovery/HEAD is unresolved. The 30-second bound and critical-path dependency are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: This scenario is materially faster and constitutes a recorded regression fix; no review finding applies to the intentional one-root filesystem probe itself.

Scenarios.Scenario: Attach an Issue or Pull Request from the editor chat context picker in a multi-root workspace
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening the attachment picker snapshots workspace folders and known Git repositories, presents one folder-level choice, then dispatches the extension command. Only an unresolved selected folder crosses into direct filesystem resolution; known repository ids skip it. GitHub search follows resolution.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Execute the extension-host GitHub context command with the chosen repository id or folder URI.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One command for the one chosen folder; no command is sent if a multi-root quick pick is cancelled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same command ran with a repository string or no scope; the core picker deduplicated repositories rather than preserving folder identity.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The attachment cannot be created until this returns.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve an unresolved selected folder through local Git config.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero for known repository ids; one direct root probe for the selected unresolved folder.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Unresolved folders were not passed through for direct config resolution and could fall back to an unscoped repository picker.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks opening the scoped GitHub search picker for that selection.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Search GitHub for scoped issues or pull requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initial request plus debounced query requests, independent of total workspace roots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same search existed, potentially under a different or unscoped repository selection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Populates the picker after folder resolution.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Workspace folder count F and known repository count R control the in-memory O(F*R) matching; only one selected folder reaches command and filesystem/network boundaries.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Folder/repository matching is synchronous and serial. The user makes one selection; repository resolution then GitHub search are serial. There is no per-root boundary fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Known Git metadata acts as the warm path and passes a repository string without filesystem work. An unresolved selected folder has no direct-config cache. Search behavior is unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: tests cover distinct repositories, duplicate repository ids across roots, and unresolved roots, and the call path is direct.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very large multi-root workspaces make the O(F*R) in-memory scan larger, but this is a user-invoked picker and realistic root counts are low; no expensive boundary scales with all roots.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: added CPU work is bounded to a user action and boundary work remains one selected folder, not all roots.

Scenarios.Scenario: Filter files through remote content exclusions during completion, prompt construction, workspace/text search, or code review
Scenarios.CriticalPath: isCopilotIgnored awaits repository resolution and policy loading before a file may be used. Review and feedback paths use Promise.all across changed files; text search can enqueue checks for every hit; completion and prompt paths await checks before producing context.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Preflight `workspace.fs.stat` on every local URI before Git discovery/API lookup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One newly added stat per uncached local file check; concurrent startup/search/review collections can therefore issue N stats for N files even when all files belong to one repository.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Callers immediately joined one shared discovery promise; opened repositories then resolved from Git API state without filesystem I/O. Only the pre-existing no-repository fallback performed a later stat.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each ignore verdict awaits the stat, and aggregate workflows await all verdicts before progressing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read up to 1 KB of a file when repository or organization regex rules require content matching.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one read per uncached file requiring regex evaluation, limited to 10 concurrent reads and keyed by content/rule scope afterward.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical limited file-content reads occurred before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing content-rule evaluation waits for this read.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch repository/organization exclusion policies from the Copilot API/GitHub-backed endpoint.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One effective fetch per missing remote after coalescing, grouped 10 remotes per request with at most five batches in flight; warm rules avoid requests for 30 minutes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same coalesced, batched policy loading existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A file verdict waits only for the policies of its effective repository and the non-git scope.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: On a warm known repository, root metadata and per-file verdict caches eliminate Git lookups. Before Git discovery settles, verdicts are intentionally not memoized, so effective new preflight-stat cardinality is N for N checked local files, including repeats; collection call sites can make N concurrent.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The new pre-discovery filesystem stats have no limiter or per-URI coalescing and can fan out to caller concurrency (for example all changed files under Promise.all, or all queued text-search jobs). Policy network requests are separately coalesced by repository, batched 10 repositories per request, and limited to five concurrent batches. Regex-triggered file reads are limited to 10.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm `_repoRootCache` reduces repository resolution to once per repository and `_ignoreGlobResultCache` memoizes settled per-file verdicts. During cold/unsettled discovery, repository metadata is absent and negative verdicts are deliberately not memoized; successful policy rules are cached for 30 minutes and in-flight policy fetches are shared.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the added awaited stat is unconditional for file-scheme URIs, tests prove repeated lookup while discovery is unsettled, source comments establish hundreds of render-time checks, and multiple production collection paths use Promise.all.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact latency of stat varies greatly between local SSDs and network-mounted workspaces, and warm caches sharply reduce frequency after discovery; the uncached per-file mechanism and unbounded caller concurrency are not uncertain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity I/O boundary fan-out; the accepted finding is anchored to the added preflight stat.

Scenarios.Scenario: Build ignore patterns for workspace search by bulk-loading discovered Git roots, and resolve workspace organization metadata
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Search pattern generation first discovers `.git/HEAD` files, then loadRepos resolves every discovered root before policy patterns are available; searches explicitly wait for this. Workspace organization resolution calls the same Git API for only the first workspace folder before any network fallback.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Search for `.git/HEAD`, then stat/read direct Git config for each discovered repository root.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One root-resolution probe per discovered repository D, all launched together; normal roots require root and `.git` stats plus one config read, with extra pointer reads for worktrees.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Root resolution waited for shared Git discovery and then used an opened Git API repository or the existing stat/getRepositoryRoot/config fallback; it had no pre-discovery worktree-aware direct read.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Workspace search waits for the complete ignore pattern, so all D root resolutions complete first.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch exclusion policies for effective remotes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Deduplicated per remote, grouped by 10 and limited to five concurrent batches; warm rules eliminate requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same endpoint, batching, cache, and limiter.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Pattern generation waits for required rules before starting the dependent search.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fall back to fetching the user's GitHub organizations if local repository remotes and token organization metadata do not identify one.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one organizations request for the first workspace folder resolution path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same fallback request followed getRepositoryFetchUrls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The caller waits for organization selection, but the network fallback is unchanged.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Bulk pattern generation scales with D discovered repository roots after search deduplication; organization resolution is one root. Each root is passed once to getRepositoryFetchUrls.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: loadRepos invokes repository resolution for all D roots with Promise.all, so direct config probes run concurrently. Subsequent policy network work is batched 10 per request and limited to five batches. Organization resolution is serial.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: loadRepos populates the repository-root metadata cache and policy rules then use the normal 30-minute cache/coalescing. Direct Git-config bytes themselves are not cached. Organization resolution has no method-local cache shown.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for boundary placement and concurrency; net cost relative to the Git API root lookup is workload-dependent.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: D can be large in workspaces containing many nested repositories, but the new direct probes replace slower discovery/root-resolution work and remain one per discovered root; no evidence establishes a net regression in this bulk-root scenario.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: direct root probing is appropriate for root inputs and can shorten the critical path, while the reported bug is specifically its unconditional application to file inputs.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all seven changed files and transitive Git, picker, ignore, search, review, filesystem, IPC, and network paths. Submitted one medium boundary-fan-out finding for the unconditional per-file filesystem stat and recorded the PR's high-confidence fix for the prior 30-second discovery wait.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
